title: BootNotificationRequest
description: Sent by a station to the server after boot to register itself, report firmware/hardware info, and declare capabilities.

firmwareVersion.description: Semantic version of the station firmware.

stationModel.description: Model identifier of the station hardware.

serialNumber.description: Unique serial number of the station unit.

bayCount.description: DEPRECATED (since 0.11.0, removed in 0.12.0): use bays instead. A scalar count cannot express a non-dense bay set and cannot carry program ordinals. Retained for one release so a station built against 0.10.0 still validates. When both are present bays is authoritative and bayCount MUST equal bays.length. Maximum bay count per controller is 64 (Chapter 01 — Architecture §4.2).

bays.description: The station's RE-DECLARED PHYSICAL TOPOLOGY — the same bays and program ordinals it declared at provisioning, restated on every boot so the server can detect that the two no longer agree. Labels are NOT re-declared and are NOT compared: they are descriptive (Chapter 04 — Protocol Flows §2), and comparing them would put a station into Pending for a corrected typo in a firmware constant. The declaration MUST be STABLE between boots while the hardware is unchanged; how firmware achieves that — NVS, a compiled-in table, a hardware scan — is its own business, and the contract is the stability, not the mechanism. A MISMATCH in either direction against the provisioned topology puts the station in Pending, NOT Rejected: Pending keeps the command channel open so an operator can repair the disagreement, and Rejected would remove the only channel through which it could be repaired (Chapter 05 — State Machines §1, station state machine). Provisioning creates the bays and boot never does, so a FIRST boot always matches unless the provisioning declaration and this one disagree — which is the same mismatch and the same Pending. A faulted bay or program is re-declared present-but-unavailable, never omitted: omission means the hardware changed and requires re-provisioning. At the 64-bay and 32-program maxima this field is under 8 KB, far below the 64 KB MQTT Maximum Packet Size of Chapter 02 — Transport §1.2.

bayNumber.description: The station-assigned ordinal identifying this bay physically, as declared at provisioning. Unique within the message. The set need NOT be dense.

programNumbers.description: The programNumber of every program this bay has, as declared at provisioning. Ordinals only — the label is not restated here, because it is descriptive and is not compared. Order carries no meaning; the server compares this as a SET. The set need NOT be dense.

uptimeSeconds.description: Seconds elapsed since the station last booted.

pendingOfflineTransactions.description: Number of offline transactions queued for synchronization.

timezone.description: IANA timezone identifier of the station (e.g. 'Europe/London').

bleSupported.description: Whether the station supports BLE communication.

offlineModeSupported.description: Whether the station supports offline session authorization.

meterValuesSupported.description: Whether the station supports reporting meter values.

deviceManagementSupported.description: Whether the station supports the Device Management profile (configuration, firmware update, diagnostics, remote commands).

connectionType.description: Type of network connection used by the station.

signalStrength.description: Signal strength in dBm, or null if not applicable (e.g. Ethernet).
